one_line_purpose: An AI representative of Jiya Singhal that an evaluator can chat with or call, proposing and booking real meeting slots from her Cal.com calendar.
problem_solved: Provides a grounded and factual AI persona for Jiya Singhal that can answer questions about her professional background (resume, GitHub repositories) without hallucination, and also facilitate real-time meeting scheduling by interacting with her Cal.com calendar. It also offers both chat and voice interfaces for interaction.

tech_stack.storage: ChromaDB (on-disk), JSON files (Repo Cards), PDF files (resume) baked into Docker image

architecture_summary: The system features a Next.js frontend deployed on Vercel, interacting with a FastAPI backend deployed on Render. The backend handles RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) by querying a ChromaDB vector store, which contains chunks from Jiya's resume (PDF) and auto-summarized GitHub repo cards. Embeddings are generated using VoyageAI. The backend uses Google's Gemini API for LLM interactions. For scheduling, the backend integrates with the Cal.com API. Voice interactions are facilitated by Vapi, which orchestrates Deepgram STT and ElevenLabs TTS, and communicates with the backend via an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Different Gemini models (`gemini-2.5-flash` for chat, `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` for voice) are used for optimization. The RAG corpus is baked into the backend's Docker image.
key_features: AI representative of Jiya Singhal for evaluators.
Interactive chat interface accessible via a public URL.
Voice interface accessible via a phone number using Vapi.
Factual claims grounded in Jiya's resume and public GitHub repositories (RAG).
Proposes and books real meeting slots from Jiya's Cal.com calendar.
Streaming voice replies with optimized first-token latency (target 1.0s in production).
Uses `gemini-2.5-flash` for chat and `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` for voice, optimizing for groundedness and latency respectively.
Automated summarization of GitHub repositories into 'Repo Cards' using Gemini.
Includes an evaluation suite with 20 questions, LLM-judging, and PDF report generation for metrics like groundedness, relevance, and honesty.
notable_code_decisions: Pre-retrieval RAG architecture for chat, where context is injected into the user turn before the LLM call, rather than relying on an LLM-orchestrated `query_knowledge` tool.
Gemini function-calling for `get_availability` and `book_meeting` tools, resolved server-side in the backend.
Dedicated OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint for Vapi custom-LLM integration, which includes server-side tool resolution when Vapi doesn't provide its own tool definitions.
Model splitting (`gemini-2.5-flash` for chat/evals, `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` for voice) to balance groundedness and first-token latency.
Use of Voyage `voyage-3-large` embeddings for document and query embedding in RAG.
Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR) is applied after initial retrieval to ensure diversity in retrieved chunks.
The RAG corpus (ChromaDB, Repo Cards, resume.pdf) is baked into the backend Docker image for deployment.
Server-Sent Events (SSE) used for streaming chat responses and managing backend/frontend communication.
tradeoffs_and_limitations: A 20% hallucination rate (groundedness < 0.8) was observed in evaluations, primarily due to a cross-repo leak where details from one repo card (search-listings) bled into narratives about another (TradeIndia).
The `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` model used for voice has a shorter context length, which is compensated for by a voice-mode prompt addendum.
The RAG corpus being 'baked into Docker image' implies that updates to the resume or GitHub repos require rebuilding and redeploying the Docker image.
Unclear from provided files regarding detailed error handling strategies beyond HTTP exceptions for external API failures.
The frontend uses a proxy (`/api/chat`) to the backend, which adds an additional network hop for chat requests.
what_it_demonstrates: This repository demonstrates the development of an advanced AI persona system leveraging RAG, large language models (Gemini), and external API integrations. It showcases how to build interactive chat and voice interfaces, implement server-side function calling, optimize for real-time performance (e.g., voice latency), and construct a robust evaluation framework for LLM-based applications, including prompt engineering for groundedness and mitigation of hallucination.
